daily.title: Opposition growing to CAS-ordered Russia ice hockey reinstatement
daily.summary: Ice hockey's governing body says the impact of a court decision forcing it to reinstate Russia presents "significant practical and sporting challenges." Several leading nations say they won't play against Russian teams.

daily.title: Germany news: Commerce chief calls for stable US trade relations after midterms, warning that uncertainty over Trump's tariff policies remains
daily.summary: German business is pinning its hopes on greater stability in US trade relations after a midterm blow for Donald Trump. Meanwhile, Germany's automakers appear to be feeling less gloomy than in recent years. DW has more.

daily.title: Indonesia deploys troops to Jakarta after wiretapping allegations
daily.summary: Indonesian troops are being stationed in Jakarta amid wiretapping allegations implicating the president's chief of staff. Suspects are being accused of illegally tapping the president's phones.

daily.title: US midterms: Democrats win House and Senate from Republicans
daily.summary: The Democratic Party gained control of the House and Senate, delivering a stinging rebuke to US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. Follow DW's live updates.

daily.title: Hungary opens communist-era secret police files identifying informants
daily.summary: The archives name thousands of former informants who spied on citizens for the state security services during decades of one-party rule. The prime minister said "many families will now face difficult information."

daily.title: Wawira Njirum, Kenya's school feeder and German Africa Prize recipient
daily.summary: From a small fundraiser to a major enterprise, Wawira Njiru's Kenyan school feeding scheme has been more successful than she ever thought possible. She's now being awarded the German Africa Prize.

daily.title: BMW reports lower Q3 earnings as China woes mount
daily.summary: BMW reports a drop in profits in the July to September quarter amid fierce competition from China.

daily.title: Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died
daily.summary: Bear, Tiger and Tiger-Duck: The author and illustrator Janosch achieved world fame with his heartwarming children's figures. He died at the age of 95.

daily.title: South Africans vote in local elections in test for ANC
daily.summary: Failing public services, corruption and high crime rates have led to growing frustration among South African voters. That could lead to further losses for the ANC.

daily.title: What US midterm elections mean for Ukraine, Iran and elsewhere
daily.summary: Donald Trump's Republicans will no longer control the US Congress after the Democrats flipped both chambers in the midterm elections. The outcome could impact conflicts in Europe and the Middle East.

daily.title: US midterm election results: Democrats flip House and Senate. Here's what else the data tells us
daily.summary: Democrats have won the majority in both House and Senate. Vote counts are still ongoing. DW takes a look at who voted Republican, who voted Democrat and what it all means.

daily.title: India news: Election body opens door for voter reinclusion
daily.summary: The Indian poll body said no action will be taken against deleted voters for using Form 6 for re-enrolment in voter rolls. Follow DW for more.

daily.title: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
daily.summary: Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes. But does disgust shape our politics, or do our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

daily.title: US to cut nearly $4 billion in Israel military aid, Trump says
daily.summary: President Donald Trump said that the United States would still sell weapons to Israel. He added that Democratic candidates were using US military support for Israel against Republicans in the midterm elections.

daily.title: Spain transport minister offers resignation in wake of train accident
daily.summary: After two deadly train crashes this year, Spanish Transport Minister Oscar Puente has said he will step down.

daily.title: Greenland's parliament ratifies Trump's US security agreement
daily.summary: The US is set to expand its military footprint on the Arctic island, part of the Kingdom of Denmark. It follows pressure from Donald Trump earlier in the year which opened a major rift in the transatlantic alliance.

daily.title: UK's King Charles III decries 'monstrous injustice' of slave trade
daily.summary: King Charles has told leaders at a Commonwealth summit that the legacy of the transatlantic slave trade "fills my heart with horror." He did not address calls for apologies and reparations.

daily.title: Why South Africa's local elections matter
daily.summary: South Africans head to the polls on Wednesday amid water shortages, frustration with local services and questions over whether the ANC's support will keep falling.

daily.title: Ukraine war: Merz doubts Russia is serious about a truce
daily.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz met with Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Berlin. Both leaders said the EU needs to be included in peace talks with Russia. Merz also expressed doubts that Russia is serious about seeking a truce.

daily.title: China and India achieved diplomatic thaw. Now the border is flaring up
daily.summary: Indian authorities have confirmed a new border "face-off" between Indian and Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradesh, raising questions about the still fragile thaw in relations between New Delhi and Beijing.

daily.title: How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community
daily.summary: As the co-founder of the ADIRA Drag Festival, Lebanese performance artist, drag performer, DJ and cultural organizer Hassandra has become an essential part of Berlin's queer artistic landscape.

daily.title: Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
daily.summary: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

daily.title: Multiple flights to European airports targeted by bomb threats
daily.summary: The bomb threats involved two passenger planes bound for Warsaw, a Ryanair flight from London to Spain, two flights to Rome and a flight traveling from Israel to the Bulgarian capital, Sofia. No explosives were found.

weekly.title: Football: Spanish player dies on after cardiac arrest on the pitch
weekly.summary: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has died following a collision with the opposing goalkeeper. The Spanish second-division club has said it is "heartbroken" by the loss.

weekly.title: Asian Cup postponed due to Middle East conflict
weekly.summary: The Asian Cup has become the latest sporting event to be affected by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. Organizers cite "exceptional circumstances" in Saudi Arabia, which has seen several Houthi attacks of late.

weekly.title: Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
weekly.summary: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

weekly.title: Germany news: Ukraine in focus at Berlin Security Conference
weekly.summary: A security conference in the German capital is addressing defending Europe against threats from Russia. Meanwhile, Germany's justice minister wants to raise penalties for sexual offenses. DW has more.

weekly.title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
weekly.summary: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

weekly.title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
weekly.summary: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, Los Angeles voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the United States to kick the oil industry out.

weekly.title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
weekly.summary: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

weekly.title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
weekly.summary: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

weekly.title: Merz says next German president 'must be a woman' — report
weekly.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's second term is due to end in March next year. Meanwhile, Merz has called for 'digital sovereignty' in the era of AI.

weekly.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
weekly.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

weekly.title: Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
weekly.summary: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

weekly.title: Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
weekly.summary: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

weekly.title: Germany's search for a nuclear waste site
weekly.summary: Finland has become the first country with a final storage facility for nuclear waste. Germany is still searching for a site, while some countries have yet to start. Costs are expected to total many billions of euros.

weekly.title: Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
weekly.summary: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

weekly.title: Germany's Gen Z protests disrupted by violence on Saturday
weekly.summary: Nationwide protests led by young people were largely peaceful throughout the day, but reports about looting and rioting in the evening, especially in Frankfurt, overshadowed the spirit of the demonstrations.

weekly.title: Embarrassing name? How we live with names we don't like
weekly.summary: What happens when your name evokes laughter or ridicule? Research points to negative life outcomes, but some people learn to embrace unfortunate names.

weekly.title: Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

weekly.title: What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
weekly.summary: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?

weekly.title: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz has expressed hope for Korean reunification during a visit to the heavily fortified border. Meanwhile, President Steinmeier has held talks with China's Xi Jinping in Beijing.

weekly.title: Bayern Munich's Kenya friendly highlights Africa's growing pull for global sport
weekly.summary: Bayern Munich are to open Nairobi's new Raila Odinga International Stadium against Ajax as Kenya prepares for AFCON 2027. The match highlights Africa's growing sports ambitions — and questions over cost and legacy.

weekly.title: Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results
weekly.summary: German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

weekly.title: IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships
weekly.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

weekly.title: Many Turkish 'guest workers' hit by poverty in old age
weekly.summary: West Germany and Turkey signed an agreement allowing the temporary recruitment of workers on October 30, 1961. Sixty-five years on, many so-called 'guest workers' can't live from their pensions.

weekly.title: The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism
weekly.summary: From Picasso to Andy Warhol, a surprising number of artists have portrayed the German breed. But the dachshund has also at times been co-opted as a political symbol.

weekly.title: Germany's Alexander Zverev clinches tennis No. 1 ranking
weekly.summary: Alexander Zverev is the second German man, after Boris Becker, to clinch the No. 1 spot in tennis.

weekly.title: 'Star Trek' star Patrick Stewart dies age 86
weekly.summary: The Shakespearean actor landed the role of a lifetime as "Star Trek" Captain Picard. He passed away at age 86.

weekly.title: India increases growth forecast for fiscal year
weekly.summary: India's Ministry of Finance has increased its growth forecasts for the current fiscal year. But it also warned about inflation, particularly for fuel and energy, amid continued instability in the Middle East.

weekly.title: Germany seeks new head of state
weekly.summary: The question of who should become Germany's new presiden is becoming pressing. Many want to see Germany's first female head of state. Chancellor Friedrich Merz is keeping his cards close to his chest.

weekly.title: Volkswagen logs Q3 operating loss of €5.86 billion on Porsche writedown
weekly.summary: The Volkswagen Group has filed its worst quarterly performance since the height of the "Dieselgate" scandal in 2015. Share prices climbed in response, however, perhaps because the bad news was so well signposted.

weekly.title: Russia shadow fleet sanctions: Can the EU act without US?
weekly.summary: The US is reportedly considering ways to convert "dark tankers" into legitimate vessels, allowing them to transport crude oil that is not subject to sanctions.

weekly.title: Germany news: Chancellor Friedrich Merz accuses North Korea of threatening Europe's freedom
weekly.summary: Friedrich Merz, who is visiting Seoul, said North Korea is putting Europe's security at risk by sending soldiers to fight for Russia in Ukraine. DW has more.

weekly.title: European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
weekly.summary: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

weekly.title: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany's health scare highlights the need for better support for elite coaches
weekly.summary: Vincent Kompany’s health concern is a reminder that elite football's pressures affect coaches too. Better support, clearer structures and mental health safeguards are increasingly vital.

weekly.title: Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
weekly.summary: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

developing.title: Live: Fresh protests hit France amid heightened security
developing.summary: Police and elite security forces are out in force in French cities as thousands participate in a new round of protests. The protest location was changed last minute in Paris. Follow DW.

developing.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
developing.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.
